data.content_ref: inline:SRC_03 identifies 'discrepancy-driven discovery' (finding unlisted errors) as the marker of genuine gain. But this criterion is both too strong and misaligned with the problem's requirement. It is too strong because genuine reliability can occur under perfect checklist compliance with no unlisted-variable discovery: if the checklist exhaustively captures the objective verification criteria and the panel applies it correctly, reliability is real even though every error found was prompted. SRC_03's own countercondition (exhaustive checklist) exposes this, yet the target offers no fallback marker. It is also misaligned because the problem asks for evidence within a single evaluation, while 'discrepancy-driven discovery' is a process-level behavior whose absence does not establish mere compliance, nor whose presence is necessary for genuine gain. Thus it fails to provide the distinguishing evidence the problem demands.
